test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 4 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Let x, s² be the mean and variance of a random sample taken from a normal distribution with mean (μ) and standard deviation (σ). Then which of the following is/are parameter/s?
solution:
The correct answer is **Both μ and σ. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In statistics, a parameter is a numerical value that describes a population characteristic. In the given scenario, x and s² refer to the sample mean and sample variance, respectively. These are statistics calculated from the sample data and are used to estimate the population parameters.
 
• On the other hand, μ represents the population mean, which is the true average value of the variable of interest in the population. σ represents the population standard deviation, which describes the variability of the variable in the population.

**Since μ and σ are population parameters that characterize the underlying normal distribution, they are considered as the parameters in this case.**
